producer.nose: Dark stone fruit with caramelized sugar and toasted oak.
producer.palate: Big oak balanced by dark vanilla and fruit.
producer.finish: Velvety, long and complex, with caramelized barrel character and baking spice.
producer.summary: Official Maker's Mark notes as relayed by the KY Supply Co. retailer blog (2023 release article), not fetched from makersmark.com.

critics.nose: Deeper and more pungent than other Maker's expressions; berry/mulberry fruit with mint and rosemary.
critics.palate: Dark caramel and chocolate, then baked berry, apple and apricot with brown sugar; no drying astringency.
critics.finish: Sweet, maple-syrup tinged, long without lingering too heavily; complexity tapers a bit.
critics.summary: Called it close to flawless and the new flagship of the range; inaugural 2023 release at 115.7 proof.

critics.nose: Toffee and somewhat astringent sawdust, buttered toast, clove and orange.
critics.palate: Dark chocolate and bitter orange moving to butterscotch, tobacco and cinnamon, then bitter oak with caramel and faint mint.
critics.finish: Oak-dominated and hotter than expected, briefly sweetened by the wheated mash.
critics.summary: Found it too oak-heavy; suited to fans of double-oaked, overproof styles. 2023 release (115.74 proof).

facts.age: Blend of 11- and 12-year-old bourbon (sources disagree on the split)

notes: Matches 2023 inaugural release at 115.7 proof. Age split conflicts: KY Supply says 70% 11yr/30% 12yr, VinePair says 13% 11yr/87% 12yr. Producer notes are retailer-relayed; makersmark.com product page 404.

critics.nose: Caramel and cinnamon up front with corn sweetness, black pepper and green apple.
critics.palate: Seasoned oak, cinnamon, brown sugar, burnt orange peel, vanilla, prune and leather.
critics.finish: Warm and lingering; cinnamon, baking and rye spice over charred oak and molasses.
critics.summary: Calls it a must-have for its proof, flavor and value.

critics.nose: Sharp rye prickle, baking spice, caramel and baked apple with a youthful grainy undertone.
critics.palate: Cinnamon and spiced honey with tarragon and mint; thick but hot.
critics.finish: Lingering peppery burn; vanilla and toffee under heat, tobacco tannins and char.
critics.summary: Excellent value at about $20 but would benefit from more age.

notes: No producer notes: oldgranddad.com redirects to a domain-sale page. Older 2014 Breaking Bourbon review skipped (score unclear).

critics.nose: Light char and oak with fresh bread and caramel.
critics.palate: Earthy cocoa, leather and apple with mild pepper; char, burnt sugar and gentle oak.
critics.finish: Burnt sugar with very mild oak.
critics.summary: Amateur blog review of the 86-proof bottling; praised its smoothness and value. No numeric score.

notes: Kansas label is the older 86-proof version; brand moved to 90 proof (~2021) and most reviews (Breaking Bourbon, The Whisky Study) cover 90 proof, so they were excluded. Producer pages 404/blocked. Only critic is an amateur blog.

critics.nose: Sweet vanilla first, then orange and vibrant oak, marshmallow, maple, milk chocolate, baking spice.
critics.palate: Orange candy and warm vanilla with oak, bread, pear, coriander, cinnamon and maple.
critics.finish: Clean, not aggressive, sweet and moderately fading.
critics.summary: 2024 release reviewed at 107 proof, 6 years old.

critics.nose: Sweet popcorn, white peach, light grain, white pepper, faint oak.
critics.palate: Rye spice, hot cross buns, mixed peppercorn, tannic oak, light brown sugar.
critics.finish: Bold rye spice, leather, dry oak, green peppercorn, lingering dry spice.
critics.summary: 2024 release at 107 proof; interesting concept but premium price limits appeal.

critics.nose: Spiced nuts, ballpark peanuts, new oak, baking spice and dried apricot.
critics.palate: Layered rye spice with cinnamon stick, tannic oak and grilled glazed peach.
critics.finish: Brown sugar giving way to bold rye spice, peppery oak and leather; dry with building heat.
critics.summary: 2025 release at 105 proof; $100 price called hard to justify. Rating not clearly captured.

notes: PROOF MISMATCH: Kansas label says 100 proof, but reviewed releases are 107 (2024) and 105 (2025); no 100-proof edition found. Critics cover the same product line at different batch proofs. No producer notes found (heavenhilldistillery.com blocked).

producer.nose: Fresh ginger, butterscotch and salt spray.
producer.palate: Salted caramel, chocolate and tropical fruit.
producer.summary: Official notes from the Jefferson's Ocean page; barrels are aged aboard ships.

critics.nose: Mature bourbon: spice, caramel, vanilla, brown sugar, cherry, orange zest, dark honey, oak.
critics.palate: Bourbon spice and dark fruit with cinnamon and cherry, plus a subtle salty brine.
critics.finish: Medium-long with caramel, wood, salt and vanilla; called very unusual.
critics.summary: Batch 21 at 45% ABV; skeptic won over by the concept.

critics.nose: Floral notes with salted caramel, soft salt and light smoke.
critics.palate: Floral, citrus and light black pepper, then caramel with faint salt and smoke, dry oak.
critics.finish: Light dry oak with dominant caramel.
critics.summary: Batch 14; salt and smoke faded with time in glass; questioned the impact of sea aging.

notes: Ocean is released in numbered voyages/batches; critics reviewed batches 21 and 14, Kansas label voyage unknown. Producer page gives no proof; 45% ABV from Whiskey Jug.

critics.nose: Oak and cedar spice over deep caramel toffee, chocolate, cola, honeycomb and baking spice.
critics.palate: Dry and brash: oak, cedar, grass, butterscotch and bittersweet chocolate.
critics.finish: Medium length, smooth, with lingering dry spice.
critics.summary: Very Old bottling at 45.1% ABV; praised character and balance.

critics.nose: Popcorn, vanilla, raisin, butterscotch, peach and subtle ginger.
critics.palate: Chewy; hickory-smoked oak with salted butter, toffee, sweet corn, caramel and fruitcake spice.
critics.finish: Buttery popcorn, cinnamon and hot ginger building to a long peppery end.
critics.summary: Sampled 2014; 45.1% ABV bottling.

critics.nose: Deep caramel, vanilla, grassy rye spice and dark fruit.
critics.palate: Viscous and fruity: orange peel, floral vanilla, deep toffee.
critics.finish: Long and warming with caramel-dipped orange and white pepper.
critics.summary: 90.2-proof Very Old; a clear step up from Very Small Batch.

notes: Kansas label (90 proof) matches the older 90.2-proof 'Very Old' Reserve. Current producer page describes a reformulated 8-year, 96-proof Reserve, so its notes were not used. Age claims vary (Difford's lists 12-17 yrs) so left null.

producer.nose: Balanced oak with fruit and dried apricot.
producer.palate: Sweet start, then white pepper spice from the high-rye recipe, with caramel and fruit.
producer.summary: Retailer (Seelbach's) product description, likely producer copy but not explicitly attributed; describes blending younger and older barrels.

critics.nose: Creamy caramel, light vanilla and oak with developing rye spice.
critics.palate: Heavy rye spice, green peppercorn, aged oak and vanilla.
critics.finish: Dry oak and leather with lingering woody rye spice.
critics.summary: Close to over-spiced but pleases spice lovers; competitive at $45. Rating not clearly captured.

critics.nose: Heavy rye spice, cinnamon, brown sugar, raisin-brandy, pine and apple cider.
critics.palate: Cinnamon candy spice with molasses cookie and baked apple; oak subtle.
critics.finish: Allspice, clove, citrus, tobacco and oak tannin held together by molasses.
critics.summary: Good entry point to the brand.

facts.region: Distilled in Indiana; Smoke Wagon is a Nevada brand

notes: Producer notes are retailer-relayed and unattributed.

producer.summary: Retailer (Seelbach's) description attributed to Smoke Wagon: rich and sweet with a very thick mouthfeel, likened to milk and cookies; proof cited around 115-116.

critics.nose: Floral and fruity: carnation, jammy cherry/raspberry, vanilla, cereal, noticeable ethanol.
critics.palate: Cinnamon, butterscotch, stewed apple and oak, moving to caramelized fruit and malt.
critics.finish: Long, creamy and chocolatey with lingering brown sugar.
critics.summary: August 2021 release; impressive complexity and integrated oak.

critics.nose: Caramel with an herbal edge, licorice, vanilla, candied pineapple, baked apple, oak, cinnamon, clove.
critics.palate: Caramel with earthy/herbal twist, vanilla, dried orange peel, baked apple, oak and spice.
critics.finish: Roasted oak, honey, vanilla cream, licorice, apple and pear.
critics.summary: Batch 14 at 57.1% ABV; rated 'Top Shelf' (top category).

notes: Batch-strength product; Kansas label is 116.4 proof but reviewed batches were 57.1% ABV and a 2021 release in a 110-120 proof range. Producer description retailer-relayed.

producer.nose: Candied apple and smoked cherry wood.
producer.palate: Acidic and zesty, with orange curacao and candied ginger.
producer.finish: Coats the tongue and throat with a warming sensation.
producer.summary: Barrell's official notes as relayed by One More Dram's launch article (press release).

critics.nose: Crisp leaves, nectarine, caramel sauce, coffee cake, cinnamon.
critics.palate: Peach, spiced syrup, oak, rye spice, creamy vanilla; creamy mouthfeel.
critics.finish: Rye spice, leather, dry oak, baking spice, hint of tobacco leaf.
critics.summary: Strong blending; finish less memorable; worth the $85.

critics.nose: Green apple with caramel, tropical fruit, white pepper, chili powder and floral notes.
critics.palate: Caramel, butterscotch, maple, praline, then cooked apple, cherry, orange marmalade, milk chocolate, coffee and toffee.
critics.summary: Accessible yet deep for both casual and seasoned drinkers.

facts.age: Blend of 8-15 year bourbons (Indiana 8/11/12, Kentucky 10, Tennessee 13/14/15)

notes: Exact batch match. Producer notes press-release relayed (Barrell shop page 404).

critics.nose: Sweet caramel, vanilla and toffee layered with nutmeg and oak.
critics.palate: Creamy, with honey and orange sweetness, spice and seasoned oak.
critics.finish: Heat spike, mild dryness, trailing caramel and spice with subtle smoke.
critics.summary: Easy-to-enjoy crowd-pleaser at its price.

critics.nose: Peanut, banana bread, hazelnut and sweet earthiness.
critics.palate: More rye-led than typical Wild Turkey; honey and milk chocolate with an odd savory sweetness.
critics.finish: Banana and milk chocolate with oak dryness and citrus.
critics.summary: Not a favorite but well put together.

facts.cask: Filtered through American white oak charcoal then Texas mesquite charcoal

notes: No producer notes: Wild Turkey Longbranch product page 404.

critics.nose: Candy corn, caramel, vanilla frosting, lemon zest, toasted oak, clove, rye spice, black cherry.
critics.palate: Caramel, vanilla, seasoned oak, graham cracker, light tobacco, black pepper, orange chocolate.
critics.finish: Rye spice and peppery oak with cinnamon, brown sugar, nutmeg and slight bitterness.
critics.summary: Better than standard 101, though the price bump may not justify it for everyone.

critics.nose: Dark roasted caramel, toasted vanilla, roasted oak, cinnamon, clove, dried grass, nuts.
critics.palate: Roasted caramel and vanilla, oak, cinnamon, nutmeg, cocoa, licorice, apple and orange.
critics.finish: Oak, coffee grounds, cinnamon, clove, burnt caramel and vanilla.
critics.summary: Export (Japan) bottling at 50.5% ABV; rated 'Mid shelf+'.

notes: Breaking Bourbon says the 8-year 101 became a US line extension after being export-only; Whiskey Shelf reviewed a Japan bottling. No producer page found (404).

critics.nose: Brown sugar, pralines, new leather, apricot, pepper and young creamed corn.
critics.palate: Caramel, brulee sugar, orange peel, cinnamon, lumber, peanut brittle, black pepper.
critics.finish: Medium length with vanilla wafer and ripe tangerine.
critics.summary: Graded A-.

critics.nose: Caramel, vanilla and pepper over roasted peanut, honeyed nougat and jalapeno cornbread.
critics.palate: Echoes the nose plus black pepper, vanilla cream, mint and circus peanut.
critics.finish: Medium-length, spicy and sweet.
critics.summary: Solid youthful everyday bourbon for sipping or mixing; Gold Medal.

facts.age: NAS; blend of 4-year in-house and 7-year sourced bourbon (per 2019 review)
facts.mash_bill: Limestone Branch distillate blended with sourced Kentucky bourbon

notes: Producer site had no product notes. Drinkhacker's age breakdown is from 2019 and may have changed.

Could not identify a Hardin's Creek 'Low Distillation' release at 109 proof; the Beam current-releases page lists only the 110-proof 2025 Warehouse Series, and hardinscreek.com was unreachable. Possibly a newer release not yet indexed.

producer.palate: Caramel and honey with a hint of agave from the tequila barrels.
producer.finish: Long and warm, with spice and sweetness.
producer.summary: Notes presented as producer notes on the Wooden Cork retailer page (retailer-relayed). Master Distiller John Rempe described the anejo-cask finish as bringing bourbon full circle (quoted via Whiskeyfellow).

critics.nose: Earthy oak, smoky vanilla, cherry, toffee, leather and agave.
critics.palate: Creamy; smoky vanilla, lime zest, nutmeg, dark chocolate, black cherry, oak spice, tobacco, agave.
critics.finish: Long; oak spice, nutmeg, dark chocolate, black cherry, old leather, cinnamon.
critics.summary: 'Bottle' rating; tequila notes complement rather than dominate.

critics.nose: Pine and oak with lemon zest, some bitterness and heat.
critics.palate: Toffee and nougat with pine and oak.
critics.finish: Astringent at first, returning to toffee.
critics.summary: Letter grade B-; bitter streaks detract, though not bad.

critics.nose: Bright, sweet and delicate: soft grain, waffle cone, lemon peel, subtle agave.
critics.palate: Vanilla, butterscotch, agave, orange peel, clove, barrel char.
critics.finish: Long; raisin, macadamia, agave, citrus peel, grapefruit, char.
critics.summary: Called it a lovely bourbon with a well-integrated tequila-cask finish; numeric score and scale ambiguous in fetch, so omitted.

facts.age: Blend of 14-year and 7-year traditional bourbon with 10-year wheated bourbon

notes: Producer tasting notes are retailer-relayed only.

producer.summary: Distillery describes it as elegant, fruit-driven and sweet, good neat, on the rocks or in cocktails; relayed by the Seelbach's retailer page.

critics.nose: Caramel, vanilla, oak and pear; traditional bourbon aroma.
critics.palate: Oak, pepper, trail mix, banana; thin and quite oaky.
critics.finish: Oak and pepper, dry.
critics.summary: Surprisingly oaky for 4 years; expected more from the blended mashbills.

facts.mash_bill: Blend of 60% corn/20% rye/20% malted barley and 51% corn/20% rye/20% malted barley/9% wheat

notes: Producer statement is a brief retailer-relayed summary only (no nose/palate/finish).

producer.summary: Producer notes quoted by The Whiskey Shelf: bold and spicy at first, mellowing to sweet caramel and maple, likened to an oatmeal raisin cookie.

critics.nose: Fruit-forward: cherry candy, orange jelly, raisin, light brown sugar, subtle oak.
critics.palate: Light-bodied; cherry, orange, lemon, vanilla, brown sugar, cinnamon, clove, leather.
critics.finish: Slightly bitter citrus and dry oak with cherry, vanilla and creme brulee.
critics.summary: Versatile and approachable.

critics.nose: Molasses-like sweetness turning to grass, charcoal and nutmeg.
critics.palate: Smooth caramel with spicier notes.
critics.summary: Balanced; somewhat pricey but worth trying.

critics.nose: Shy; grassy, nougat caramel, vanilla, pine, maple.
critics.palate: Brown sugar, dried apricot, vanilla, roasted oak with a grainy, cracker-like harshness.
critics.finish: Honey, fennel, roasted oak, dried apricot; dry and spicy.
critics.summary: Rated 'Mid Shelf'; disappointed, drinks like a cheaper bottle.

facts.cask: Maple charcoal filtered (Lincoln County Process); charred new American oak

notes: Producer notes are second-hand (quoted in a review); Uncle Nearest product page 404.

producer.summary: Jack Daniel's says it is bottled straight from the barrel at full proof (125-140), with intensified vanilla and toasted oak; robust but not overpowering.

critics.nose: Maple sugar candy and banana over burnt wood; inviting smoke.
critics.palate: Chocolatey caramel, burnt wood, pipe tobacco, banana, nuts; drinks lower than its proof.
critics.finish: Bold, spicy, near-tannic heat that fades to burnt wood and maple.
critics.summary: Barrel at 130.6 proof; recommended despite barrel variation. Rating not clearly captured.

critics.nose: Banana bread, toasted marshmallow, deep caramel, faint salted almond.
critics.palate: Praline pecan, overripe banana, buttery biscuit; little heat.
critics.finish: Oak tannin, dry leather, dark chocolate and charred marshmallow.
critics.summary: Rural Inn store pick at 135.7 proof.

facts.cask: Single barrel, barrel proof (125-140 proof range)

notes: Single-barrel product, so each barrel differs; Kansas label is 129 proof, reviews are of 130.6- and 135.7-proof barrels. Mash bill omitted (sources disagree on rye vs barley split).

critics.nose: Fresh and vegetal with mint and oak.
critics.palate: Grain and earth, then raisin, cinnamon and caramel.
critics.finish: Smooth and mellow.
critics.summary: Enjoyable for all experience levels.

critics.nose: Banana nut bread, caramel, maple, light cinnamon and vanilla.
critics.palate: Brown sugar and maple, nuttiness, banana and vanilla; little oak.
critics.finish: Graham cracker, vanilla, brown sugar; moderate length, minimal burn.
critics.summary: Big step up from the 80-proof standard but not exciting.

notes: No producer notes (Jack Daniel's Bonded page 404).

critics.nose: Clean and crisp: green apple, honey, cinnamon, caramel, corn, orchard fruit, char.
critics.palate: Honey, apple, corn, apricot, rye spice, caramel, wood, pine-mint.
critics.finish: Medium; caramel, honey, spice, wood and mint.
critics.summary: Praised drinkability and balance; a repeat purchase for the reviewer.

critics.nose: Banana with vanilla, like bananas foster.
critics.palate: Weightier than Jack Daniel's, light maple-syrup feel with apple and oak spice.
critics.finish: Slightly bitter on ice, with fruit and oak spice.
critics.summary: Good in cocktails, especially a mule.

notes: No producer notes found. Whiskey Jug score omitted (scale unclear in fetch).

producer.summary: Official notes relayed by BroBible: fruit-forward with heavy nut character; charcoal mellowing gives a creamy mouthfeel.

critics.nose: Dried corn, brown sugar, oak, caramel, baking spice, leather, dried cherry, vanilla.
critics.palate: Mirrors the nose: dried corn, caramel, oak, cinnamon, leather, tart cherry.
critics.finish: Long; dried corn, oak, caramel and spice.
critics.summary: Summed up as spiced caramel corn; recommended neat or in a Manhattan. Letter-grade style rating (B+ range), numeric score omitted.

notes: Whiskey Wash review of Fall 2008 skipped: it covered the earlier 11-year release. Whiskey Shelf 13-year review was a 2005 distillation, skipped. Producer notes relayed by BroBible.

critics.nose: Crisp apple, white peach, cedar, vanilla, light syrup.
critics.palate: Caramel and brown sugar, baking and rye spice, vanilla, oak.
critics.finish: Vanilla, oak, leather, white peppercorn, brown sugar.
critics.summary: Well-rounded Washington bourbon that holds up to Kentucky at 90 proof. Rating not clearly captured.

critics.nose: Grain, hay, lactic sourness, cashew, lemon, puff pastry.
critics.palate: Light and gently sweet: honey, custard, nutmeg, baked apple.
critics.finish: Sweet and chewy.

facts.age: NAS (5 years per company, via Breaking Bourbon)

notes: No producer notes: Woodinville shop lists finished variants; plain straight bourbon page not found.

producer.summary: Producer page: rich texture with sticky baked plum and chocolate-covered cherry; finished six months in Douro Valley port barrels.

critics.nose: Vanilla, blueberry, raspberry, seasoned oak.
critics.palate: Raspberry, grape, caramel, dark chocolate; good mouthfeel.
critics.finish: Plum, grape, seasoned oak, light leather, dry port aftertaste.
critics.summary: Sweet, fruit-forward daily drinker; dry winey finish holds it back.

facts.cask: Finished about six months in port barrels from the Douro Valley

notes: Producer gives a descriptive summary rather than split nose/palate/finish.

producer.nose: Honey-drizzled apple slices, verbena, fresh-cut grass, saddle leather and cinnamon.
producer.palate: Tart orange and lemon candy, pound cake, sugar cookie, smoky baking spice, honeysuckle.
producer.finish: Long; smoky tobacco turning to caramel apple with walnut and cinnamon.
producer.summary: Official Garrison Brothers notes; grain-to-glass Texas bourbon aged in intense heat.

critics.nose: Raw grainy corn, caramel, sweet tea, cigar wrapper, leather, maple.
critics.palate: Chocolate, leather, charred oak, butterscotch pudding, honey candy; little baking spice.
critics.finish: More oak; chocolate, leather, caramel, honey, coffee liqueur.
critics.summary: Worth trying once for wheated-bourbon fans.

critics.nose: Maple gingerbread, toasted sesame, vanilla, toasted oak, marzipan, herbs.
critics.palate: Butterscotch, spiced pine, maple, chocolate-chip pancake, dried mango.
critics.finish: Slightly tannic and oaky in a flavorful way.
critics.summary: 3-year-old at 94 proof; Gold Medal (archived 2023 review).

facts.mash_bill: Corn, wheat and barley (74% corn, 15% wheat, 11% malted barley per Bourbon Culture)

notes: Mash percentages and age come from critics, not the producer page.

critics.nose: Raisin and oak, cereal, faint cinnamon and baking spice, char.
critics.palate: Baking spice and rye warmth, coffee and leather bitterness, char; creamy.
critics.finish: Creamy with straw.
critics.summary: Standout in the Balcones range; drinks rye-like.

critics.nose: Sawdust and oak spice, then honey, vanilla, toffee, canned peach, apricot jam, cocoa.
critics.palate: Spicy charred oak and toasted nuts, then vanilla, creamed corn, cooked apricot, stewed apple.
critics.finish: Long, spicy and drying; clove, cocoa, sandalwood.
critics.summary: Called it delicious with great structure.

facts.mash_bill: Roasted blue corn, Texas wheat, Texas rye, malted barley

notes: No producer notes (balconesdistilling.com fetch not permitted).
